prompt:
You are a decision-support tool for a radiologist. Review this patient's frontal chest X-ray and report on six findings. A radiologist checks your output; give your best assessment. Findings and their definitions: - Lung Opacity: airspace opacity, consolidation, infiltrate or airspace disease in the lung. A discrete nodule or mass is not Lung Opacity (it is Lung Lesion). - Cardiomegaly: an enlarged heart. A borderline or upper-normal heart size counts as absent. - Atelectasis: collapse or incomplete expansion of lung tissue, including subsegmental or plate-like atelectasis. - Lung Lesion: a nodule, mass or cavity in the lung. A calcified granuloma does not count. - Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space. - Fracture: a fracture of the ribs, clavicles, spine or any other visible bone. Healed or old fractures count. How to work: 1. Read the patient's image systematically first. 2. Then look at the 10 most similar cases from a reference database, listed below with their reports. They are other patients whose images look similar to this one. Use them as supporting evidence to confirm or question what you see in the patient's image, not as the answer: a finding in a similar case does not mean that this patient has it. 3. Take the clinical indication into account. 4. For each of the six findings, give its status (present, absent or uncertain), the probability (0 to 1) that it is present in this patient, the IDs of the similar cases that support your call (an empty list if none), and a rationale of one or two sentences. Then give a short impression. Do not explain what the findings are. Cite cases by their ID exactly as written, e.g. CXR316. Give the probability with two decimals as your honest estimate; for subtle, borderline or partly obscured appearances, use intermediate values rather than a fixed low value. Clinical indication: XXXX-year-old male with dizziness. Similar cases (most similar first): Case CXR929 (similarity 0.977): FINDINGS: No change lung XXXX. XXXX opacities are present in the right lower lobe. No focal infiltrates. Heart and mediastinum are unremarkable. Aorta normal. IMPRESSION: Findings of COPD with right lung base focal atelectasis. No evidence for failure or pneumonia. Case CXR1084 (similarity 0.976): FINDINGS: The trachea is midline. The cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal. The lungs are clear, without evidence of acute infiltrate or effusion. There is no pneumothorax. The visualized bony structures reveal no acute abnormalities. Case CXR1145 (similarity 0.976): FINDINGS: Lungs are hyperexpanded. There is no focal airspace consolidation. No suspicious pulmonary mass or nodule is seen. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Normal heart size and mediastinal contour. IMPRESSION: 1. No focal air space consolidation. 2. Hyperexpanded lungs, suggestive of emphysema. Case CXR3371 (similarity 0.974): FINDINGS: Heart size within normal limits. Negative for focal pulmonary consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. Calcified right hilar lymph XXXX noted. IMPRESSION: No acute abnormality. Case CXR1636 (similarity 0.973): FINDINGS: Lungs are clear. No pleural effusions or pneumothoraces. Heart and mediastinum of normal size and contour. IMPRESSION: Clear lungs. Case CXR2192 (similarity 0.971): FINDINGS: No focal lung consolidation. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion.Heart size and pulmonary vascularity are within normal limits.Minimal degenerative changes of the thoracic spine. The previously
described XXXX deformity in the midthoracic spine is again seen. There is subcutaneous shunt catheter tubing along the anterior chest wall IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary process. Case CXR1854 (similarity 0.971): FINDINGS: The cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal in size and contour. No focal consolidation, pneumothorax or large pleural effusion. Negative for acute displaced rib fracture. IMPRESSION: Negative for acute abnormality. Case CXR3025 (similarity 0.970): FINDINGS: The lungs are clear bilaterally. Specifically, no evidence of focal consolidation, pneumothorax, or pleural effusion.. Cardio mediastinal silhouette is unremarkable. Visualized osseous structures of the thorax are without acute abnormality. No acute displaced rib fractures. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.. Case CXR1822 (similarity 0.970): FINDINGS: The heart is normal in size and contour. There is no mediastinal widening. No focal air space disease. Prominent hilar XXXX. No large pleural effusion or pneumothorax. The XXXX are intact. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormalities. Case CXR986 (similarity 0.968): FINDINGS: The lungs are clear. There is no focal airspace consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size and mediastinal contour are normal. IMPRESSION: No evidence of active disease. The patient's frontal chest X-ray follows.
